newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UK's Lasmo gets new licences in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: UK's Lasmo gets new licences in Pakistan.

text.p: Britain's Lasmo plc said on Tuesday it had secured three new licences to explore for oil and gas in southern and southwestern provinces of Pakistan.

Joe Darby, chief executive of Lasmo, accompanying British Prime Minister John Major on a visit to Pakistan, told Reuters the licences were for three years of seismic studies and exploration in two blocks in the southwestern province of Baluchistan and one block in the southern province of Sindh.

"Work on the licences will start soon. In the first year we will review the seismic studies and in the second year do new seismic studies," Darby said, adding that sites for exploration wells would be decided in the third year.
The licences are for onshore and offshore exploration in Bela North, Bela South in Baluchistan and Kirthar in Sindh.
Darby said that Lasmo had applied in December for new offshore licences in the Indus Delta, but could not say when Pakistan might take a decision on that.
In 1996 Lasmo and Britain's National Power Plc jointly signed a memorandum of understanding with Pakistan to conduct a feasibility study on importing liquefied natural gas.

Darby said phase one of the project had been completed and a report presented to the government. Phase two had also been completed but the report had yet to be completed. "The study will hopefully be presented by end of February," he said.
Lasmo began exploring for oil and gas in Pakistan in 1987 and has invested $240 million with local partners to develop the Kandanwari gas field.
